references.text: God elaborates on his self-revelation by identifying himself as the God of the fathers—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—and thus links 'I AM' to the covenant name YHWH.
God reveals his name YHWH to Moses and explains that he did not fully make himself known by this name to the patriarchs.
God declares, 'I am he, yes I am he' (אֲנִי אֲנִי הוּא), a similar self-revelation that confirms his unique existence and sovereignty.
God calls himself 'the First and the Last' and declares, 'I, the LORD, am the First,' reflecting the eternal self-existence found in 'I AM WHO I AM.'
God declares, 'I am he' (אֲנִי הוּא) and 'Before me no god was formed, nor shall there be any after me,' emphasizing his eternal being.
The LORD declares himself to be the First and the Last, and that there is no God besides him—an elaboration of divine self-existence.
God says, 'I am he; I am the First and I am the Last,' reflecting the eternal 'I AM' revelation.
God's name 'Lo-Ammi' (not my people) contains an implicit reference to the covenant formula and God's 'I AM' as their God.
Jesus says, 'ἐὰν γὰρ μὴ πιστεύσητε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι' (for if you do not believe that I AM), using the divine self-revelation expression.
Jesus says, 'τότε γνώσεσθε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι' (then you will know that I AM), linking himself to God's self-revelation in Exodus 3:14.
Jesus declares, 'πρὶν Ἀβραὰμ γενέσθαι ἐγὼ εἰμί' (before Abraham was born, I AM), a direct claim of divine preexistence with reference to 'I AM.'
When Jesus says, 'ἐγώ εἰμι' (I am he), the soldiers fall to the ground—a reaction suggesting the divine power inherent in this name.
The Lord God says, 'ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος' (the One who is and who was and who is coming), an expansion of the 'I AM' revelation to past, present, and future.
The four living creatures praise God as 'ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος' (the One who was and who is and who is coming), reflecting God's eternal being.
Exodus 6:2 clarifies and confirms God's identity as 'I AM' from 3:14 by linking it to the name YHWH.
